memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The LORD reigns for ever and ever." - Ex 15:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Six words, and the song ends.

Think about who is singing this and what they have just watched. For four
centuries, Pharaoh reigned over them. Pharaohs came and went, each one absolute
in his own lifetime, each one certain of his permanence. Egypt built pyramids to
make its rulers last.

Now Israel stands on a shore where the latest Pharaoh's army lies drowned, and
they sing: the LORD reigns for ever and ever.

Every human power has an expiry date. That is not cynicism; it is simply
observation. The regimes that seem unshakeable are all temporary, and the people
living under them rarely believe it at the time.

This is a steadying truth when the world feels out of control. Whoever holds
power today does not hold it permanently, and none of them hold it outside God's
authority. Daniel says God "sets up kings and deposes them" (Dan 2:21).

The book of Revelation lands on the same note as this song: "The kingdom of the
world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Messiah, and he will reign
for ever and ever" (Rev 11:15).

Israel sang it by a sea. We will sing it at the end of all things.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What power in the world troubles you that will not last?
2. Does God's eternal reign comfort you or unsettle you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You reign for ever and ever. Steady my heart when the world feels
uncertain, and let me live under Your rule today. Amen.
